# Task: world

## Goal

Turn the skeleton's empty rectangle into the §3 sea: an authored tile map with four small islands, shoals and docks, ships that sail with acceleration, braking and turning and cannot cross land or shoals, docking at island docks, and a sight radius that the server enforces, so no client receives ships it cannot see (§16). Browsers show the map, their own view of nearby ships and a fogged minimap.

## Context

- Read `docs/spec.md` §3 (sea and islands: movement, visibility, travel-time targets), §2 ("Spawn fairness"), §16 ("Hidden information") and §17 ("Content definitions": tile-editor maps, validators). Read `docs/architecture.md` and the skeleton code it maps, especially `packages/simulation` (integer state, `step`, `hashState`), `packages/content/src/sea.ts`, `apps/server/src/MatchRoom.ts` and `schema.ts`, and `apps/web`.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration`, `npm run build` (ending with `scripts/smoke-build.ts`) and `npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`. Playwright's Chromium for `@playwright/test` 1.63.0 is installed and shared read-only; never run `playwright install`.
- Another feature (`duel-core`) runs at the same time and adds `packages/simulation/src/duel`, `packages/content/src/moves`, `packages/test-tools/src/replay` and subpath exports in those three packages' `package.json`. Never create or edit those paths or those three `package.json` files, so the two branches merge cleanly.

## Constraints

- Keep the skeleton's rules: integer fixed-point simulation with no floating-point transcendental functions in the pure packages (an integer heading table written as literal data or generated by a script is fine), the server as the only writer, zod-validated protocol messages, and the private-match admission layers. Change the protocol version, since input changes.
- Use existing tooling: Colyseus `StateView` (or its 0.18 equivalent) for per-client visibility, Phaser for drawing, zod for data validation.
- The map is authored as a Tiled JSON map (`.tmj`, a documented subset) under `assets/source/maps/`. A script under `scripts/` converts it into a typed TypeScript module in `packages/content/src/`. The content package's tsconfig stays unchanged, so do not import JSON directly. A unit test fails when the generated module is out of date with the source map.
- Placeholder art only: coloured tiles and shapes drawn by Phaser, no image files.
- Out of scope: walking on islands, ruins, rubbings, loot, rumors, encounters, fruit, economy, match phases.

## Acceptance

- Map content, validated by unit tests that fail on a broken map:
  - four small islands, each with at least one dock; shoals as obstacles; eight spawn slots on the outer sea;
  - every dock and spawn slot reachable by sea;
  - at full speed on the shortest sea path, neighbouring islands 20–40 s apart and the longest useful crossing at most 90 s;
  - adjacent spawn slots out of engagement range (a named content constant).
- Sailing, unit-tested in `packages/simulation`: throttle forward accelerates to a maximum speed, braking decelerates, turning changes an integer heading at a turn rate, and a ship never enters a land or shoal tile. A collision stops or slides the ship without tunnelling, including at full speed. Docking works with interact near a dock at low speed: it stops the ship and records the dock; any throttle undocks. The whole state stays integer, and the determinism test still holds.
- Visibility, proven on real clients: an integration test with headless clients shows that a ship outside the sight radius is absent from the other client's decoded state, appears when it sails within the radius and disappears when it leaves. A player's own ship is always visible, and terrain needs no sync because the map is static content.
- Browser: the web client draws the tile map, follows the player's ship with the camera, lists and draws only visible ships, shows the docked state in the HUD, and has a minimap whose fog clears around the player's path (client-side is fine, as terrain is public). The four browser scenarios in `policy.json` pass: `join-private-match`, `two-ships-sync`, `sail-and-dock`, `out-of-sight`.
- Tests may place ships deterministically through a test-only server setting, for example an environment variable read only by the dev and test entry points. It is off by default and documented, and it never weakens admission or visibility.
- `docs/architecture.md` describes the map format and pipeline, sailing, docking and the visibility boundary, still within about a page and a half. `README.md` mentions the map script.
- `npm ci` then each of the five policy checks passes from a clean checkout.

Browser checks: each scenario id appears in exactly one test title as `[scenario:<id>]`. That test, when it passes, attaches exactly one image/png named `screenshot:<id>` (other attachments are fine). The verifier refuses anything else. Before completing, run the spec files you changed with a JSON report:

```bash
WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=worker PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_FILE=<tmp>/report.json \
  npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts --reporter=json <spec files>
```

Then check the report with the verifier's own rules: run the exact `check-report` command the controller appends to this task when it pins it.

## Stop

Report `blocked` instead of continuing when any of these happens:

- `npm ci` or an install fails twice for reasons outside the repository (registry, network).
- Colyseus 0.18 offers no per-client state filtering that keeps other ships out of a client's payload.
- A check can pass only by changing a path outside the owned paths.
- After two and a half hours of work, any required check still fails and you cannot name the next fix.

Report `question` only for a choice that would change this acceptance.

# Pirate Sea Race

A browser multiplayer pirate treasure race. The specification is `docs/spec.md`, the text of `docs/spec.docx`; section numbers (§) below refer to it.

- Stack: TypeScript everywhere. Phaser renders the client (`apps/web`), Colyseus runs the authoritative server (`apps/server`), and a pure fixed-step simulation (`packages/simulation`) is shared by both. The layout follows §17.
- Build and test commands (from the repository root, Node 24): install `npm ci`; develop `npm run dev` (server on 2593, web on 5393); check `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration`; build `npm run build` (then `npm start` runs the built server); browser `npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`.
- Authoritative logic (`packages/simulation`, `packages/protocol`, `packages/content`) never imports Phaser, Colyseus, DOM APIs, wall-clock time or `Math.random`.
- Boundaries: never change `docs/spec.docx`, `docs/spec.md` or anything under `features/`.

## Workflow (operator notes; workers skip this section)

Features under `features/` run with md-manager's workflow controller (`~/dev/md-manager/workflow`, documented in its README.md and RUNBOOK.md). The `workflow` command on PATH wraps `~/dev/md-manager/.venv/bin/python -m workflow`. With no `--repo` flag, it targets this repository.

- Interview: `/workflow-grill <feature>` writes `features/<feature>/decisions.md`. Commit the feature files before launching.
- Check: `workflow launch <feature> --dry-run`.
- Launch in a new Herdr tab: `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-opus-5-5 workflow launch <feature> --live --automatic --worker-timeout-seconds 10800 --review-timeout-seconds 3600`. Reviewers then run as native sessions in their own panes. The design challenge is always a headless print job: it prints nothing until its verdict, so never interrupt it.
- Runs are stored in `~/.local/state/agent-workflows/project-B/<feature>/<run-id>`. `workflow status|answer|resume|repair` take that run path.
- Workers run targeted tests only; the controller's verifier runs the full policy checks.
- Update Claude Code between runs, never during one. After an update, restart long-lived Claude sessions (preflight names the stale ones).
- This VPS (4 cores, 7.9 GB) fits 3–4 worker lanes, and one full test suite plus one or two Playwright runs at a time.

content.content:
status paused

- P1 assumption | decisions.md says the build check's smoke step "proves the new subpath exports resolve from dist/". It doesn't. `scripts/smoke-build.ts:24-31` loads a hard-coded `WORKSPACE_EXPORTS` list that holds only the six existing root specifiers. `scripts/` is outside the lane's owned paths, so the worker can't add `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/duel`, `@pirate-sea-race/content/moves` or `@pirate-sea-race/test-tools/replay` to it. Two things are left partly checked. The simulation build (customConditions []) type-resolves `content/moves` through its `types` path. If the replay runner imports `simulation/duel`, the test-tools build does the same for that path. Nothing checks any `default` runtime path, and nothing checks `test-tools/replay` at all. Unit tests run before build and use the source condition, so they can't catch it either.

- P2 failure_mode | `packages/test-tools/package.json` declares no dependency on `@pirate-sea-race/simulation`. The owned-path rule allows only adding subpath exports to that file. Declaring the dependency would also need `package-lock.json` (a root file) to change, or `npm ci` may reject the out-of-sync lockfile. The replay runner will work as an undeclared import through the hoisted workspace symlink. The build also works because `npm run build --workspaces` runs in array order: simulation is built before test-tools.

- P2 assumption | The input assumption (horizontal direction already an integer in {-1,0,1}) conflicts with the acceptance item 'both horizontal directions together are neutral'. The step can't receive 'both held' as input, so the step can't test this rule. The existing `PlayerInput` (`packages/simulation/src/input.ts`) also uses a [-1000,1000] axis, not {-1,0,1}. `duel-online` will build its adapter against whatever shape this feature freezes.

- P2 failure_mode | The −12 on block and jab-punish test holds only in a narrow case: the heavy connects on its first active frame, and the jab still reaches after blockstun pushback. Pushback and the hitbox reach are the worker's choice. With 16 sub-pixels per pixel, a small pushback can easily carry the defender past jab range. Mirroring integer boxes by facing ([x, x+w) vs (−x−w, −x]) can also introduce a one-unit asymmetry.

- P2 failure_mode | The order-independence acceptance ('both fighters' hits evaluated before a KO, independent of player order') is easy to satisfy in form but not in fact. Examples: a single loop that applies P1's hit and then checks P2's hit against the updated state, throw-vs-throw on the same frame, throw vs strike on the same frame, or a stamina guard break computed in sequence. None of these same-frame cases is settled by the rules as written.

- P2 complexity | The four baseline moves' timings already live in `packages/content/src/frameBudgets.ts` with their own validator. The new `moves` data will restate startup, active, recovery and block advantage, and its validator will duplicate the 'block advantage beyond active + recovery' rule.

- P2 assumption | The step takes (config, state, inputs), but the snapshot holds only the state. Nothing ties a snapshot to the move data or rules it was produced under.

SIMPLER: Keep the whole duel in one step module in `packages/simulation/src/duel`, with the replay loop as a pure `replay(config, initial, inputs)` function beside it. `packages/test-tools/src/replay` then only parses and validates the JSON log format and calls that function, so the determinism and rollback tests can live in simulation with no cross-package import. For move data, derive the four §8 baseline moves from `baselineFrameBudgets` instead of retyping them. Give each move one hitbox rectangle for its whole active phase, and each fighter a fixed hurtbox per stance (standing, crouching, airborne) instead of a per-frame timeline. That satisfies 'integer hitboxes and hurtboxes' and the validator with far fewer places for off-by-one mirroring and pushback bugs. Add a per-frame timeline later if `duel-online` playtests need it.

EXPERIMENT: In a scratch copy of the base commit (about 5 minutes):
1. Add a `"./duel"` subpath export that follows the existing pattern to `packages/simulation/package.json`, with a one-line `src/duel/index.ts`.
2. Add `"@pirate-sea-race/simulation": "0.0.0"` to `packages/test-tools/package.json` dependencies.
3. Run `npm ci`. If it fails as out of sync with the lockfile, the replay runner must use the undeclared hoisted import.
4. Run `npm run build`, then `node -e "import('@pirate-sea-race/simulation/duel').then(m => console.log(Object.keys(m)))"`. This shows whether the export pattern resolves from dist, and confirms that nothing in `npm run build` would have caught a typo in it.

Together these settle whether `scripts/smoke-build.ts` must join the owned paths before launch.

# Decisions: duel-core

From the operator session of 2026-09-24 (slice planning after the skeleton merged into `main`), revised after design challenge attempt 1 of duel-core-001 by the assistant under the operator's standing instruction to finish the run.

## Decisions

- Scope is the pure duel simulation only (slice 1 of the plan). Networking, the arena client and the duel room are the next feature, `duel-online`, which builds against this feature's API from `main`. The API therefore has to be usable without changes: a step function, a snapshot that is plain data, and a pure replay function.
- One lane (`duel`). Duel rules and move data are too coupled to split, and a split lane would fail its isolated typecheck against the other's types.
- Only the Duelist kit. Fruit kits (§9) come with the content slice; the Duelist's two specials are the advancing thrust and the counter slash.
- Haki abilities (§10: Armament, Observation parry, Resolve finisher) and the Haki meter are deferred. The spike's exit (§18: guard, punish, throw, simultaneous hit, reconnect) doesn't need them, and they add balance work before the core is proven.
- Units: integer sub-pixels, 16 sub-pixels per arena pixel. Positions, velocities, gravity and hitboxes are integers; hitboxes and hurtboxes are axis-aligned rectangles relative to the fighter's origin and facing.
- The code lives in new directories behind subpath exports (`@pirate-sea-race/simulation/duel`, `@pirate-sea-race/content/moves`), so this feature edits no existing file. `world-sea` runs at the same time on the rest of the repository, and the two branches must merge without conflicts.
- No browser check: nothing is rendered. The policy's checks are typecheck, unit, integration (unchanged, to prove nothing broke) and build.
- Proving the build output (challenge P1): `scripts/smoke-build.ts` hard-codes the existing exports and `scripts/` is not this lane's (the policy can't change without a new run, and `world-sea` owns `scripts/`). So each of the two packages proves its own new subpath with a `postbuild` script that imports it from `dist/` without the source condition. Adding the two subpaths to `smoke-build.ts` is left for the merge or a later feature.
- The replay runner is a pure `replayDuel` in `packages/simulation/src/duel`, with the log's zod schema in `packages/content/src/moves` (challenge P2). `packages/test-tools` would need a new dependency on `simulation`, and so a lockfile change, and the lockfile belongs to `world-sea` in this parallel pair. `duel-online` can wrap `replayDuel` in `test-tools` later. This departs from §17's "test-tools: replay runner" for now.
- Simplified collision data (challenge's simpler alternative): one hitbox per move for its whole active phase and one hurtbox per stance. Per-frame timelines wait until playtests need them.
- Same-frame rules the spec leaves open, decided here: detect everything against start-of-frame state and apply together; throw against throw breaks both with no damage; an active strike beats a throw in startup or active; stamina and guard breaks use start-of-frame stamina. A mirrored-players symmetry test guards order independence.
- The duel input carries held directions as separate left/right/up/down bits, so the step resolves both-horizontal to neutral (§8) and `duel-online`'s adapter passes keys through unchanged.
- The four §8 baseline moves take their timings from `baselineFrameBudgets` and reuse `moveTimingSchema`, and the duel state records `MOVESET_VERSION` so a snapshot is never replayed against other move data.

## Assumptions

- The arena is one plane with two walls and a floor; its width is content data. There's no stage hazard and no ring-out.
- A duel input per player per frame is a button bit field (light, heavy, special one, special two, dash) plus integer horizontal and vertical directions in {-1, 0, 1}, already as §8 maps keys. Keyboard mapping is client work.
- Frame data for moves outside §8's table (launcher, anti-air, the two specials) is the worker's choice within §7's ranges, documented in the move data.
- `hashState` from `packages/simulation` is reused for duel state, which also holds the duel's own frame counter and generator state if it needs one.
- The duel starts both fighters at fixed positions, facing each other, with full health and stamina, as §6 requires ("no free opening hit").

## Deferred

- Haki meter and abilities (§10), fruit kits (§9), focus scrolls.
- Networking, prediction and reconciliation, the input delay policy, reconnect: `duel-online`.
- Rendering, animation, the duel HUD and control remapping: `duel-online`.
- Hosting the duel inside `MatchRoom`, reservations, transitions and theft: `encounters-theft`.

The worker stayed inside the owned paths: all 18 changed files are under `packages/simulation/src/duel`, `packages/content/src/moves`, the two `package.json` files or `docs/duel.md`. No dependencies were added. File:line references are at 7282786.
  
  ## P1
  1. **The buffer swallows throws (item 2).** `step.ts:363` starts a throw only when light and heavy are both in the buffer on the frame the fighter is free. `step.ts:369` starts the jab as soon as light arrives alone, and consumes it. I checked this with a scratch run: J and then J+K one or two frames later gives "8 hit jab" and no throw. The 4-frame buffer only helps a throw pressed while the fighter can't act. `duel.test.ts:362-379` tests the buffer with light only.
     *Fix:* delay a lone light or heavy on a free fighter by 1–2 frames (a small throw window) until the other button can arrive, and add a J→K test at 1 and 2 frames.
  2. **A whiffing strike beats a throw (item 3).** At `step.ts:73-74`, `strikeActive` (`step.ts:196-201`) ignores overlap and `moveHit`. I checked it with a crafted state: a jab facing away from a thrower whose throw is active and in range. The result was no grab, no hit and no events. The throw test at `duel.test.ts:276-281` uses a jab that also connects, so it can't tell the two apart.
     *Fix:* cancel the grab only when `contacts[other]` is a hit or block (or run the overlap test ignoring `moveHit`). Add a test with a facing-away or out-of-range active strike.
  
  ## P2
  3. **`separate()` tie-break keyed to slot.** `step.ts:417`: when x is equal and both facings are equal, `a.facing` puts the slot-0 fighter left or right, so the mirrored run differs. `awayFrom` (`step.ts:184`) pushes both fighters the same way in that case. It is rare (same x on landing).
     *Fix:* break the tie by velocity or previous x, or document it and test it.
  4. **`MOVESET_VERSION` is hand-maintained.** It is the string `"duelist-1"` (`duelist.ts:8`). A hash pin in `determinism.test.ts:128` guards only the shipped data. At runtime only strings are compared (`step.ts:55`, `snapshot.ts:19`, `replay.ts:47-48`), so a custom moveset that keeps the version string passes.
     *Fix:* derive the version from a content hash of the data.
  5. **`restoreDuel` checks only the top-level shape** (`snapshot.ts:22`).
     *Fix:* validate fighters with a zod schema before stepping.
  6. **The move types are written twice.** `DuelMove` and `DuelMoveset` are hand-written interfaces (`schema.ts:32-133`) that sit beside the schemas, and `parsed.data as DuelMove` (`schema.ts:305,310`) hides any drift. `sameTiming` (`schema.ts:290-301`) compares fields by hand.
     *Fix:* use `z.infer` types, or add a type-level equality check.
  7. **Three `as unknown as Pair<FighterState>` casts** (`step.ts:142,145,157`).
     *Fix:* use a typed `pair(fn)` helper.
  8. **The symmetry test doesn't check that its trades happen.** `determinism.test.ts:218` asserts only which event kinds occur, not that a same-frame double hit or trade happened.
     *Fix:* assert that the frame-21 jab trade gives both fighters a hit event.
  
  ## Checks
  - **Punish test (item 1): strong.** The two cases are the corner at the heavy's maximum reach, `cornered(1279)`, where the wall moves the attacker back the full 64, and midscreen with the defender walking back (`duel.test.ts:389-409`). It asserts the gap is at most 1343, the jab lands before the attacker is free, and 1280 whiffs. The jab reach limit is exactly 1343 (<1344), so the margin is zero but correct.
  - **Same-frame resolution (item 4):** all detection reads the start-of-frame fighters. Results apply in one `map`, and stamina and guard break read start-of-frame stamina (`step.ts:286`). Apart from P2 #3 there is no slot tie-break. The mirrored script (`determinism.test.ts:182-208`) includes a simultaneous jab, a throw clash, escapes, cross-ups and 600 random frames, and it compares whole states on every frame.
  - **Imports (item 6):** simulation imports only `@pirate-sea-race/content/moves`, its own `../hash.js` and `../fixed.js`, and vitest. It has no `zod` import and no undeclared imports.
  - **Postbuild (item 7):** real. The scripts at `simulation/package.json:25` and `content/package.json:28` self-resolve with plain `node` (no source condition), require a `/dist/.../index.js` path, and check for `stepDuel` / `MOVESET_VERSION`. Workspace order builds content first.
  - **Purity (item 8):** only `Math.max/min/abs`. There is no random, Date, timer, DOM or transcendental maths. `/ 2` in `state.ts:117-118` is safe because the validator requires even values and `isSafeInteger` guards the result. Integers are enforced by a test that runs `canonicalize` on every state (`determinism.test.ts:113`).
  - **Acceptance (item 9):** everything is covered except the throw-input and whiff cases above. That includes clock, timeout, overtime and draw, double KO, KO on the last frame, KO in either slot order, guard levels, stamina costs, regen timing, guard break (30 frames, 30 stamina, from start-of-frame stamina), scaling 45/36/29/22/18, the 5-hit knockdown, left+right and up+down neutral, and escapes for both slots.
  - **Docs and reuse (item 10):** `docs/duel.md` is accurate and short, but it doesn't mention the counter slash's strike invulnerability, or that a throw needs light and heavy pressed on the same frame.
  
  ## Good patterns
  - Baseline timings are taken from the table itself (checked with `toBe`, `moves.test.ts:56-60`), and `moveTimingSchema` is reused.
  - The validator rejects start positions within reach of any move, which matches §6's "no free opening hit".
  - Pushback against a wall moves the attacker back instead.
  - Deep-freeze test proves the step never mutates its input.
  - Snapshot restore and replay are tested with a JSON round trip at frames 0, 1, 1234, 3599 and 3600.
  - Replay refuses logs from another moveset version or a different start frame.
</agent-message>

# Task: duel

## Goal

Fix what the review of run duel-core-001 found in the duel simulation on this branch: a keyboard player must be able to throw, a strike that misses must not cancel a throw, and the rollback contract must be airtight (slot-neutral separation, a moveset version derived from the data, fully validated snapshots). Everything else about the duel stays as it is.

## Context

- This branch contains duel-core-001's result. `features/duel-core/duel-task.md` and `features/duel-core/decisions.md` still define the duel, and all of it still applies. Read `docs/duel.md` first, then `packages/simulation/src/duel/step.ts`, `snapshot.ts`, `replay.ts` and `packages/content/src/moves`.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build`; the packages' `postbuild` self-checks must keep passing.
- The `world-sea` feature may still be running on the rest of the repository. Stay inside your owned paths.

Findings to fix (P1 are required):

1. (P1) Throw input. `step.ts` starts a jab as soon as `light` is buffered alone (around line 369), so pressing J and then K one or two frames later gives a jab, never a throw. Keyboard rollover rarely lands both keys on the same 60 Hz frame. Give a free fighter a short chord window (one or two frames, a named rule constant): a lone light or heavy waits that long for its partner before it starts, and light plus heavy within the window is a throw.
2. (P1) Whiff beats throw. The throw-cancel check (around lines 73–74) uses `strikeActive`, which is true "whether or not it reaches". A jab facing away or out of range therefore cancels a connecting throw. Cancel a throw only when the opponent's strike actually hits or is blocked on that frame.
3. (P2) `separate()` breaks an exact tie (equal x and equal facing) by slot, so a mirrored run can differ. Break it without reference to the slot (for example by previous x or velocity), and cover it with the symmetry test.
4. (P2) `MOVESET_VERSION` is the hand-written string `"duelist-1"`. Derive the version that snapshots and replays carry from the move data itself (for example `hashState` of the moveset), so changed data can never keep an old version.
5. (P2) `restoreDuel` checks only the top-level shape. Validate every field of a restored state (types, integer ranges, known move ids, both fighters) before it is stepped, and refuse anything else.
6. (P2) `DuelMove` and `DuelMoveset` are hand-written beside their zod schemas and joined with `as` casts. Derive the types with `z.infer` (or prove equality at the type level). Replace the three `as unknown as Pair<...>` casts in `step.ts` with a typed helper.
7. (P2) The symmetry test doesn't assert that its scripted trade happens. Assert that the same-frame jab trade gives both fighters a hit event.
8. (P2) `docs/duel.md` doesn't mention the counter slash's strike invulnerability or the throw chord window. Add both.

## Constraints

- Owned paths as in `policy.json`. Change only what these findings need, keep the existing structure, names and patterns, and keep every existing test passing unless a finding says it is wrong.
- Pure, integer, deterministic, as before. No new dependencies.
- Changing input timing (finding 1) changes replays. Update the recorded determinism fixtures and hash pins deliberately, and say so in `docs/duel.md`.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests: J then K at 0, 1 and 2 frames apart from a free fighter all give a throw, and a lone J gives a jab after the chord window. An active strike facing away or out of range doesn't cancel a connecting throw, and one that connects still does. The exact-tie separation is slot-neutral under the mirrored symmetry test. A restored snapshot with any malformed field is refused. Changing any move datum changes the moveset version, and a snapshot or replay from the old data is refused.
- All the duel-core acceptance still holds, including determinism over 3,600 frames, rollback replay and the `postbuild` self-checks.
- `npm ci` then the four policy checks pass from a clean checkout.

## Stop

Report `blocked` instead of continuing when any of these happens:

- `npm ci` or an install fails twice for reasons outside the repository (registry, network).
- A check can pass only by changing a path outside the owned paths.
- After ninety minutes of work, any required check still fails and you cannot name the next fix.

Report `question` only for a choice that would change this acceptance.

# Decisions: duel-core-fixes

From the operator session of 2026-09-24, written by the assistant under the operator's standing instruction to finish slices 1 and 2. The findings come from the assistant's review of duel-core-001's diff; the official reviews of that run are merged in below when they add anything.

## Decisions

- This is a follow-up feature on top of duel-core-001's result, not a new run of `duel-core`: the lane changes only what `duel-task.md` lists, and reviewers review this diff.
- Throw input: a free fighter holds a lone light or heavy for a short chord window (one or two frames, a named rule constant) before starting it, so a keyboard J+K with ordinary rollover becomes a throw. The cost is one or two frames of extra startup on a free fighter's lone light or heavy. This is the usual fighting-game answer, and §8 asks for rollover to be checked.
- A throw is cancelled only by a strike that hits or is blocked on the same frame, never by an active hitbox that misses.
- The moveset version is derived from the move data (a hash), not written by hand.
- One lane (`duel`) with the same owned paths as `duel-core`, so it can still run beside `world-sea`.

## Assumptions

- The replay fixtures and hash pins change because input timing changes; that is expected and documented.
- The chord window applies only to a fighter that can act; the existing 4-frame buffer still covers inputs made during recovery.

## Deferred

- Haki, fruit kits and the other duel-core deferrals stand.
- Adding the new subpath exports to `scripts/smoke-build.ts`: done when `world-sea` (which owns `scripts/`) is merged.

new=old+"""

Found by the official reviewers of duel-core-001 (general and coverage):

9. (P2) A guard break sets stamina to 30 (\`step.ts\`, around line 289: \`Math.min(maxStamina, guardBreakStaminaRestore)\`). §7 says a guard break "restores 30 stamina": add 30, capped at the maximum.

11. (P2) The guard-break test (\`duel.test.ts\`, around line 327) probes only the cost threshold from a fresh state. Also cover a guard break after regeneration timing matters, and the stamina restored by a break."""
assert s.count(old)==1; s=s.replace(old,new)
old2="- Unit tests: J then K"
s=s.replace(old2,"- Unit tests: a guard break adds 30 stamina capped at the maximum; the opening-hit validator rejects a moveset whose advancing special reaches from the start distance. J then K",1)
open(p,"w").write(s)
p="$D/decisions.md"; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("- The moveset version is derived","- A guard break adds 30 stamina, capped at the maximum: the plain reading of §7's \"restores 30 stamina\" (duel-core-001 set it to 30).\n- The moveset version is derived",1)
s=s.replace("The findings come from the assistant's review of duel-core-001's diff; the official reviews of that run are merged in below when they add anything.","The findings come from the assistant's review of duel-core-001's diff (both P1s, which the official reviewers missed) and from the official general and coverage reviews of that run.",1)
open(p,"w").write(s)

Add the duel-core-fixes feature for duel-core-001's review findings

A keyboard throw (J then K a frame or two apart) always became a jab, and
an active strike that missed still cancelled a connecting throw. Both P1s

# Task: world

## Goal

Deliver the `world-sea` feature with its review findings fixed. Run world-sea-001 built it and passed every check, but its coverage reviewer blocked the candidate because nothing proves the client draws the tile map, and its general reviewer never finished. Start from that run's snapshot, then close the findings below so that the whole feature can be reviewed again.

## Context

- `features/world-sea/world-task.md` and `features/world-sea/decisions.md` define the feature; all of it still applies. Read them first.

- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration`, `npm run build` and `npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`. - `duel-core` is already merged on `main`, and `duel-core-fixes` may be running. Never create or edit `packages/simulation/src/duel`, `packages/content/src/moves`, `packages/test-tools/src/replay` or the `package.json` of `simulation`, `content` or `test-tools`. Keep the exports of `hash.ts`, `fixed.ts`, `random.ts`, `frameBudgets.ts` and `rules.ts` (`formatIssues`, `ValidationResult`) unchanged, because the duel code imports them.

Findings to fix:

1. (coverage, P1) No test checks that the web client draws the tile map. `SeaScene.createTerrain` (`apps/web/src/seaScene.ts`, around lines 97–141) is never read back, and the browser helpers sample pixels only at ship positions. Add browser assertions (in an existing scenario, keeping the scenario ids) that sample canvas pixels at a known land, shoal and dock tile, using the camera offset, and expect each tile's placeholder colour.
2. (coverage, P2) The browser check for fog is weak: `data-fog-revealed` is checked once at spawn and comes from the scene's own bookkeeping. Show in a scenario that the revealed count grows as the ship sails, and that a revealed minimap pixel changes from the fog colour.

- Keep the four browser scenario ids and the protocol version (3).

- Findings 1–8 are fixed. Finding 1 asserts real canvas pixels at land, shoal and dock tiles. Finding 2 shows fog clearing along a sailed path on the minimap. Findings 3–5 have unit tests.
- `npm ci` then each of the five policy checks passes from a clean checkout.

Browser checks: each scenario id appears in exactly one test title as `[scenario:<id>]`. That test, when it passes, attaches exactly one image/png named `screenshot:<id>` (other attachments are fine). The verifier refuses anything else. ```bash

# Decisions: world-sea-fixes

From the operator session of 2026-09-24, written by the assistant under the operator's standing instruction to finish slices 1 and 2. The run world-sea-001 passed every check, but its coverage reviewer blocked the candidate (P1: the tile map is never proven drawn) and its general reviewer was stopped before a verdict.

## Decisions

- The follow-up starts from the world base (`b8f4c37`) and restores world-sea-001's snapshot (`509e888`, `refs/workflow/e467a18ef3280d1e/world`) as its first step. The reviewers therefore see the whole world diff plus the fixes. That matters here, because no general review of the world code was ever completed. (`skeleton-fixes` instead reviewed only the fixes on top of an already reviewed candidate.)
- Scope: the coverage reviewer's P1 and P2, and six P2s from the assistant's own review of the snapshot (the dock snap sweep, the heading limit, the tile-cost constants, the route literal, the `§` encoding, the SDK-internal guard).
- The map is kept as it is: 224×208 tiles, 99.2% sea, neighbours 22–23 s apart, longest crossing 54 s at the skeleton's 5 tiles/s. The emptiness this causes (ships rarely meet with a 10-tile sight radius) is a design question for the next world slice: faster ships or a denser layout.
- The same lane, owned paths, checks and scenario ids as `world-sea`.

## Assumptions

- The assistant's review found no P0 or P1 in the snapshot. A read-only merge of it with `duel-core` (`a23b8a2`) is conflict-free and passes typecheck, unit (228) and integration (21).
- The test-only placement route stays as designed: dev entry only, 404 in production.

## Deferred

- Map density and ship speed, landmarks, the 12-island alpha map.
- Adding the duel subpath exports to `scripts/smoke-build.ts`: done when both branches are merged into `main`.

The game is running on `main`, with the server on `ws://localhost:2593` and the web client on `http://localhost:5393`. Everything was already merged, so starting it was the only step left.

From your laptop, reopen the tunnel through your SSH alias, then go to `http://localhost:5393`:

**Controls:**

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| ↑ or W | Accelerate |
| ↓ or S | Brake (slow reverse from a stop) |
| ← → or A D | Turn |
| E | Dock, when near an island dock at low speed |

lines: - **Map format and pipeline.** The map is authored in Tiled as `assets/source/maps/slice-sea.tmj`, in a documented subset of Tiled's JSON format (`packages/content/src/tiledMap.ts`): orthogonal, finite, 16 px tiles; one embedded tileset whose tiles carry a `type` of `sea`, `land`, `shoal` or `dock` (placeholder art, so the tileset has no image); a `terrain` tile layer as a plain gid array; an `objects` layer with a named `island` rectangle per island (property `theme`) and a `spawn` point per slot (properties `slot` and `facing`). Anything outside the subset is refused. `npm run map:build` (`scripts/build-map.ts`) converts it into `packages/content/src/maps/sliceSea.ts`: one string of terrain characters per row plus the islands and spawn slots. It refuses a map that fails the validators, and a unit test fails when the module is out of date with the source map (it reads the `.tmj` through a Vite `?raw` import, so the content package stays free of Node APIs).

- **Validators.** `validateSeaMap` checks §2 and §3 on the decoded map: four small islands, each land tile inside one island rectangle, every island with a dock beside its land and open sea; shoals; eight spawn slots on open sea outside the islands' bounding box and pairwise beyond `ENGAGEMENT_RANGE_TILES` (6); every dock and slot reachable by sea; and, by eight-way shortest paths that never cut a blocked corner, at full speed: each island's nearest neighbour 20–40 s away, no dock-or-slot crossing over 90 s, and a dock within 40 s of every slot. The slice sea is 224 × 208 tiles: neighbours are 22–23 s apart and the longest crossing is 54 s.

- **Sailing.** Positions are integer sub-units (256 per tile); headings are 64 directions, 0 east and clockwise because y grows down. Unit vectors come from a literal quarter-turn cosine table, so no transcendental function runs. Each world step the throttle (`-moveY`) accelerates towards 64 sub-units a step (five tiles a second), brakes, or reverses slowly from a stop; `moveX` turns one heading a step; no throttle coasts to a stop. The hull is a square of half-size 80 around the position. A move sweeps each axis in turn through the tile columns or rows its leading edge enters and stops flush at the first land or shoal (or the map edge), so a ship slides along an obstacle it meets at an angle, runs aground head-on, and cannot tunnel at any speed.

-- **Docking.** Interact (E) with no throttle, at speed 24 or less, with the ship's centre within 1.5 tiles of a dock tile's centre and a clear hull along the straight run to it (checked one sub-unit at a time, so it cannot cut a corner of land) moors it there: it moves to the dock's centre, stops, and the state records the dock's id. A moored ship ignores turning; any throttle casts off in the same step.

+- **Docking.** Interact (E) at speed 24 or less, whatever the throttle (a ship driven into its dock with ahead held docks once the shore stops it), with the ship's centre within 1.5 tiles of a dock tile's centre and a clear hull along the straight run to it (checked one sub-unit at a time, so it cannot cut a corner of land) moors it there: it moves to the dock's centre, stops, and the state records the dock's id. A moored ship ignores turning. It stays moored while E or the throttle it moored with is held (`mooredThrottle`); releasing that throttle and pressing any throttle, or pressing the other direction, casts off in the same step. The server latches a button pressed between two world steps until the next one, so a quick tap of E is never lost, and the HUD's Harbour line says "Press E to dock" or "Slow down to dock" by the same rule.

- **Visibility boundary (§16).** The room's `ships` map is tagged `.view()`. Each client gets a Colyseus `StateView` on joining; after every mirror the room puts into it the client's own ship and each ship within `SIGHT_RADIUS_TILES` (10, centre to centre, compared as integer squares by `visibleShipIds`) and takes out the rest. Colyseus then encodes no other ship into that client's patches: an integration test checks both the decoded state and the raw frames. `players` in the state is the public player count. Terrain is static content every client bundles, so it is never synced, and the minimap fog (cleared around the player's path) is client-side presentation, not a security boundary.

- **Test placement.** Tests put ships where a scenario needs them through `POST /__test/place` (code, session id, tile, heading). Only the dev and test entry (`apps/server/src/dev.ts`, used by `npm run dev` and the browser tests) reads `PIRATE_SEA_RACE_TEST_PLACEMENT=1` to offer it, and it is off unless set; the production entry (`main.ts`) never reads it, which the build smoke test checks. It moves a ship and nothing else: admission and views are unchanged.

My first fix exposed a second bug: the ship docked, but the still-held ↑ cast it off again on the next step, so the dock never stuck.

**How it works now** (commit `7fbf5a6` on `main`):
- **E docks whatever the throttle**, as long as you're within about 1.5 tiles of the dock and at speed 24 or less. Sailing into the dock with ↑ held works: the shore stops you, then E docks.
- **Once docked you stay docked** while E or the direction you arrived with is held. To leave, release ↑ and press it again, or press ↓ to back out.
- **Quick taps of E always count.** The server now remembers a press until the next world step instead of losing it.
- **A new "Harbour" line in the HUD** says "Press E to dock at …" beside a dock, or "Slow down to dock at …" if you're too fast.

**Checks on the fix:** 276 unit, 22 integration and 4/4 browser scenarios pass, plus typecheck and build. The new tests cover each rule, plus an integration test that drives in at full speed with ↑ held and taps E, exactly as you played it. The docking section of `docs/architecture.md` is updated too.

As you chose, this fix went straight to `main` without the workflow's independent review. If you want a reviewer to look at it, I can run one over commit `7fbf5a6` on its own.

# Task: duel

## Goal

Build the combat spike of §18 stage 1: two browsers fight a 1v1 duel online with the approved duel simulation, through a standalone duel room, with §15's server-authoritative prediction and rollback, and a harness that measures it under simulated latency, jitter and loss. A practice mode against a dummy lets one player try the controls. The spike's exit, "guard, punish, throw, simultaneous hit and reconnect cases are credible online", is judged by the operator's playtest after this run; this task delivers everything that playtest and the automated checks need.

## Context

- Read `docs/spec.md` §6 ("Reservation and transition": countdown, readiness), §7, §8 (controls), §12 (disconnect in a duel), §13 (duel HUD and result), §15 (all of it) and §19 ("Network and performance targets", "Combat determinism").
- Read `docs/duel.md` (the duel simulation: `stepDuel`, snapshots, `restoreDuel`, `replayDuel`, the throw chord window, moveset versioning) and `docs/architecture.md` (rooms, admission, input gate, visibility, tests).
- The duel API is `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/duel` and `@pirate-sea-race/content/moves`. Use it as it is; see Constraints for the one exception.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration`, `npm run build` (ending with `scripts/smoke-build.ts`) and `npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`. Playwright's Chromium for `@playwright/test` 1.63.0 is installed and shared read-only; never run `playwright install`.

## Constraints

- Keep the duel rules untouched: no change to what `stepDuel` computes or to the move data. You may add to the duel API (for example, helpers the netcode needs), with unit tests, but any existing test in `packages/simulation/src/duel` or `packages/content/src/moves` must pass unchanged.
- The server is the only authority on hits, health and the result (§15); clients send frame-tagged inputs only, validated with zod in `packages/protocol` like world input, with the same size, rate, sequence and future-frame limits. Bump `PROTOCOL_VERSION`.
- Duel rooms use the same three-layer private admission as matches (code or one-time create token; `onAuth` before any seat; the room's own check), and hold exactly two players, or one in practice mode.
- Keep the sea feature working: all its checks and its four browser scenarios stay green.
- Use existing tooling (Colyseus messages and reconnection, Phaser, zod, Vitest, Playwright). No new runtime dependency unless an existing one cannot do the job; pin exactly and justify it in `docs/architecture.md`.
- Tests must drive input the way players do: keys held through actions, taps shorter than a frame window, the throw chord pressed with ordinary rollover.
- Out of scope: embedding duels in `MatchRoom`, encounters, reservations from the sea, theft, fruit kits, Haki, art and sound.

## Acceptance

- **Duel room** (`apps/server`): a standalone Colyseus room per duel, created by one player with a code the other joins (and a practice variant with a server-side dummy whose behaviour can be switched between idle and guarding). # Decisions: duel-online

From the operator's grill session of 2026-09-24, after slices 1 and 2 (duel core, sea) merged into `main`.

## Decisions

- Duel entry: a standalone Colyseus duel room joined by its own code, plus a practice mode against a server-side dummy. It hosts the same duel simulation object that `MatchRoom` will embed in `encounters-theft` (§14). This keeps the spike isolated from the sea and from reservations, transitions and theft.
- Netcode: §15's server-authoritative prediction and rollback. Clients predict with the shared `stepDuel`; the server sends checkpoints and input acknowledgements, and a mismatch restores the checkpoint and replays. The shared input delay is 3–8 frames, chosen per duel from measured latency. This is the part the spike exists to prove; a plain input-delay model was rejected because its findings would not carry over.
- One fullstack lane (`duel`). A lane can't compile against another lane's new types, and the arena, the netcode and the room share new protocol types.
- The spike's exit (§18) is judged by the operator's playtest after the run: guard, punish, throw, simultaneous hit and reconnect must feel credible at §19's latencies. The run delivers the automated evidence (hash agreement and bounded corrections through the impairment harness) and the dev latency setting the playtest needs.
- The sea's density problem (224×208 tiles, 99.2% sea, 10-tile sight radius) is deferred to `encounters-theft`, where sight, speed and travel times can be tuned against real encounters.
- Tests drive input like players do (held keys, short taps, the throw chord with rollover), after world-sea's docking bug passed every check with idealised input.

## Assumptions

- Checkpoints and inputs travel as Colyseus messages over the existing reliable WebSocket; the room's synced Schema state is not used for the duel's frame data. Head-of-line stalls from loss are exactly what the harness measures.
- The duel room reuses the input gate's limits (size, rate, sequence, future frames) with a duel input schema.
- `packages/test-tools` may now depend on `@pirate-sea-race/simulation` (for the replay wrapper and the headless duel client), because this feature owns the lockfile.
- Rates the worker chooses and documents: checkpoint frequency (for example every 6 frames), the input forwarding cadence, and the correction threshold used in the harness test.
- The dummy's behaviour (idle or guarding) is a practice-mode option, not an AI.

## Deferred

- Embedding duels in `MatchRoom`, grapples and challenges, reservations and the 3-second transition from the sea, theft and respawn: `encounters-theft`.
- Haki abilities, fruit kits, art, animation and sound.
- Duel spectating (§6 defers it).
- Tuning the input-delay policy after the playtest (§15 "Tune this policy in the spike"): a follow-up if the playtest asks for it.

content.content:
- P1 failure_mode | The task requires the duel input gate to use the world gate's limits unchanged, and §15 wants one frame-tagged input per step. `InputGate.receive` (apps/server/src/inputGate.ts:36-40) counts messages in a fixed 60-server-frame window and drops the 61st. `MAX_INPUT_MESSAGES_PER_SECOND` is 60. So one message per frame leaves no headroom. Three things push a window past 60: 20 ms of proxy jitter moving one message across a window boundary; a loss stall that releases a burst of queued inputs into the next window; and a headless client on `setInterval(16.67)`, since Node fires at 16–17 ms, which is about 60–62 messages a second, not 60.
   CONSEQUENCE: Accepted inputs get dropped as rate-limited, including in the zero-impairment harness run. The server then repeats or neutralises those frames, so presses are lost (a jab or throw that never happens) and correction counts go up for reasons that have nothing to do with the netcode. The worker then either quietly raises the cap, which breaks the 'same limits' constraint, or sets a correction threshold loose enough to hide the problem. Settle this before work starts. Recommended fix: each message carries the inputs for a short run of frames (for example `{seq, frame, inputs:[…≤4]}`, which fits in 128 bytes), sent at no more than 30 messages a second, so the 60-per-second message cap and its window stay exactly as they are.

- P1 assumption | The plan never says where the rollback core lives: the history ring, prediction, checkpoint compare, restore-and-replay, correction counting and input-delay selection. The harness needs it in a headless duel client in `packages/test-tools`. The browser needs it in `apps/web`. `apps/web` is a Vite app that test-tools can't import, and a new `packages/netcode` would fall outside the owned paths. The easy path is to write the logic twice.
   CONSEQUENCE: The integration test's evidence (hash agreement, bounded corrections at 80 ms / 20 ms / 1 %) would then describe a headless reimplementation, not the client the operator playtests. That evidence is the whole point of the spike. Settle it now: the core goes in a pure module inside an owned package, for example a new `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/duel` addition or subpath. It gets unit tests, stays under the purity rules (the caller supplies time), and `scripts/smoke-build.ts` loads it from `dist`. Both the browser client and the headless client call it.

- P2 failure_mode | The check 'server and both clients agree on the final `hashState`' passes trivially if each client just restores the final checkpoint, or the result message's snapshot, before hashing.

- P2 assumption | The plan says nothing about how a client's frame counter tracks the server's: time sync, drift correction, catching up after a stall. It also doesn't say what drives the client's steps. If `requestAnimationFrame` does, a hidden tab throttles it to about 0 Hz, and a 144 Hz display runs it faster than

- P2 failure_mode | When a client's own input arrives late, the server fills that frame with a repeat or neutral. The client still holds the input it actually sent, and 'replay unacknowledged inputs' will step with that input rather than the one the server applied.

- P2 failure_mode | The impairment proxy has to behave like TCP. Per-message random jitter must never reorder messages in one direction. The 1 % loss has to become a head-of-line stall of roughly RTO length for everything queued behind it, and the random source needs a seed.

- P2 failure_mode | The `duel-online` scenario has to show the result in both views. The round clock is 60 s plus a 3 s countdown, and Playwright's per-test timeout is 60 s (tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts:16). The rules can't be shortened.

- P2 failure_mode | The keyboard throw in `duel-practice` ('J then K a frame apart') depends on Playwright timing. With two Chromium instances, Vite preview and the server on one machine, `waitForTimeout(16)` can stretch past the 2-frame chord window.

- P2 assumption | The dev latency setting has to delay the client's socket in both directions, including the RTT probes sent during the countdown. It also isn't compiled into the Vite production build that the browser checks use.

SIMPLER: Keep §15's model but narrow its surface. (1) Put a single pure rollback core in an owned package (simulation), with no timers and the caller supplying time, and use it from both the browser and the headless harness client. (2) Replace the separate input-forwarding and checkpoint messages with one server-to-client 'frame bundle' per cadence (for example every 3 frames). It carries the applied input pairs for the frames since the last bundle, including substitutions, and a full snapshot every second bundle (hash-only otherwise). The client rolls back as soon as a confirmed input differs from what it predicted, and uses the snapshot only as the authority and desync detector. (3) Send client inputs as small redundant batches at no more than 30 messages a second, so the existing 60-per-second gate and 128-byte cap stay untouched. That gives one message type, one cadence and one code path for the harness to prove.

EXPERIMENT: Before any UI work, spend about an hour on a Node script. Stand up a minimal duel room that uses the existing `InputGate` unchanged and steps `stepDuel` at 60 Hz. Run two SDK clients sending one input per frame from `setInterval`, through a 30-line FIFO delay proxy (40 ms ± 10 ms one way, plus a seeded 200 ms stall with 1 % probability per message). Over 60 s, count rate-limited drops, late inputs replaced by repeat or neutral, and snapshot bytes per checkpoint. If drops are above zero, as the fixed 60-frame window suggests, the batched-input protocol is decided before the protocol types are written. The same script also shows how many frames of input delay stop late-input substitutions at §19's 80 ms scenario.

# Task: ledger

## Goal

Build the objective ledger of §4 as pure, deterministic code: the 12 rubbings with their stable ids, where each one is at every moment, and every operation that moves one (collection, duel settlement with theft, recovery caches). It must be impossible to lose or duplicate a rubbing, which §19's first launch gate requires. Later features wire it into the match room. This one only builds and proves the rules.

## Context

- Read `docs/spec.md` §4 (all of it), §11 (the PvP gold row, rounding, "Suppress gold rewards for repeated victories"), §12 (the defeat and disconnect table and "Details that prevent exploits"), §18 (the `slice` and `alpha` presets) and §19 ("Inventory correctness", "Disconnects").
- Read `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/duel.md`, the existing pure packages (`packages/simulation`: integer state, `hashState`, the seeded generator; `packages/content`: `rules.ts` with the `slice` and `alpha` rules presets and zod validators) and `tests/unit/purity.test.ts`.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build`.
- Two other features run at the same time: `duel-online` (most of the repository) and `claim-channel` (`packages/simulation/src/claim`, `packages/content/src/claim`). Stay inside your owned paths.

## Constraints

- Owned paths only: `packages/simulation/src/objectives`, `packages/content/src/objectives`, `docs/objectives.md`, and `packages/simulation/package.json` and `packages/content/package.json` **only to add one subpath export each** (`@pirate-sea-race/simulation/objectives`, `@pirate-sea-race/content/objectives`, following the existing pattern with the `@pirate-sea-race/source` condition first). Do not change their `postbuild` scripts or dependencies, any existing source file, barrel, tsconfig or root file.
- Pure and integer like the rest of `packages/simulation`: no Phaser, Colyseus, DOM, timers, wall-clock time, `Math.random` or floating-point transcendental functions. Time is the world tick (20 per second) supplied by the caller; randomness only from a seeded generator kept in the state.
- Every operation is a function that takes the ledger state and a request and returns a new state plus a result; it never mutates its input. Requests that are duplicate, stale, unauthorised or already resolved return the current result without changing anything (§16).
- Out of scope: networking, rooms, rendering, ruins and their puzzles, rumors, shops, claims (`claim-channel`), the duel itself.

## Acceptance

- **State and invariant**: the ledger holds each rubbing's id, type and exactly one location: sealed at a source, owned by a player, held in a recovery cache, or reserved inside an unresolved duel (§4). Players hold at most one rubbing of each type. A function checks the invariant (every id present exactly once, one location each, no player holding a type twice), and every test calls it after every operation.
- **Content**: the four types (Sun, Moon, Tide, Storm) and the source assignment per rules preset: `slice` has 2 types and 8 rubbings, `alpha` has 4 types and 12 (3 of each). Assignment to islands is seeded and server-controlled, and it is zod-validated.
- **Collection** (§4): a player collects from an unlocked source by holding interact for 6 uninterrupted seconds. The ledger exposes start, progress and cancel as tick-driven operations; an interruption resets progress. A type the player already holds cannot be collected, and the rubbing stays sealed.
- **Duel settlement** (§4, §11): reserving a duel locks both players' rubbings. Settlement commits once, and validates eligibility again at commit time.
  - **Normal win:** the winner chooses one type the loser holds and the winner lacks, within a 5-second choice window. Without a choice, the default is the eligible type with the fewest free sources, then a fixed type order. The winner also takes 20 % of the loser's gold, capped at 50, rounded down and never negative. Gold is suppressed for a repeated win over the same opponent within 3 minutes, but theft still applies.
  - **No eligible type:** no rubbing moves, but the gold still transfers.
  - **Draw:** nothing moves.
  - **Repeated result message:** changes nothing.
- **Losses and caches** (§12):
  - Every loss grants the loser a fresh-rumor entitlement for the lost type (a flag the rumor system will read later).
  - When a disconnect reservation expires or a player quits, their remaining rubbings go into a recovery cache at a given position, without duplicating a rubbing that was just transferred.
  - A cache never despawns and disappears when empty.
  - Only a player missing a type can claim that rubbing from a cache, one rubbing per 6-second interaction.

import json, re
for pkg in ("simulation", "content"):
    p = f"packages/{pkg}/package.json"
    s = open(p).read()
    pattern = re.compile(r"<<<<<<< HEAD\n(.*?)=======\n(.*?)>>>>>>> [^\n]*\n", re.S)
    m = pattern.search(s)
    ours, theirs = m.group(1), m.group(2)
    # Both sides end without the closing brace of their entry; the shared closing "}" follows the markers.
    merged = ours + "    },\n" + theirs
    s = s[:m.start()] + merged + s[m.end():]
    assert "<<<<<<<" not in s and ">>>>>>>" not in s
    data = json.loads(s)  # proves the result is valid JSON
    print(pkg, list(data["exports"].keys()))
    open(p, "w").write(s)
EOF

## feature/duel-online/duel-online-001
b8c2934 Workflow duel-online-001: feature files revised after design challenge attempt 1
* P1 | The dev latency setting's actual behaviour has no test. apps/web/src/duel.test.ts:47-54 only checks devLatencyFromQuery's query parsing, and scripts/smoke-build.ts:77-87 only checks that the production bundle lacks the marker string. No unit, integration or browser test runs applyDevLatency / DelayLine (apps/web/src/devLatency.ts:26-61) to show that outgoing and incoming messages (probes included) are delayed by about rtt/2 each way, that jitter is added, or that order is kept. No e2e spec loads the page with ?rtt=&jitter=. Nothing checks that the reported RTT or the chosen input delay rises under the setting. The operator's playtest at §19 latencies depends on this setting working.

* P2 | No test checks that input delay selection follows the measured latency. The only live assertion is the local case (tests/integration/duel.test.ts:141-147: delay === MIN_INPUT_DELAY, plus at least 20 RTT samples). In the harness at 80 ms / 20 ms / 1 % (tests/integration/duelHarness.test.ts:122, 158-163), diagnostics.inputDelay is only annotated and printed; expectWithinBudget never checks it. So nothing asserts that the countdown probes measure the proxied round trip or that the room picks a delay above the minimum from it. The summary's 'input delay 3 and 7' is unchecked output. chooseInputDelay and linkStats are unit-tested in isolation only (packages/simulation/src/netcode/netcode.test.ts:

* P2 | No test checks the HUD's stamina display. apps/web/src/duelHud.ts:81-83 renders duel-stamina-<player> (data-value and --fill), but neither tests/e2e/duel.spec.ts nor apps/web/src/duel.test.ts reads it. Health bars, the clock, the connection line and the result are all asserted. Stamina is checked only on the server state (tests/integration/duel.test.ts:207), not on what the HUD shows.

* P2 | The resync-after-stall test (packages/simulation/src/netcode/netcode.test.ts:410-423) asserts only session.frame and the resyncs counter; its last assertion, expect(bundle).toBeDefined(), checks nothing. It never checks that the session's confirmed or predicted state was restored from the latest snapshot (for example hashState(session.confirmedState) === hashState(authority.state)). The snapshot is also delivered as a frame gap, so applyBundle has already restarted from it before tick() calls resync(). The case the requirement names, contiguous bundles still arriving while ticks stall (a hidden tab), so that only resync() restores the state, is never exercised with a state check.

* P2 | The stable-id de-duplication is tested only for a hit event, at the rollback level (netcode.test.ts:134-147 and 286-299). No test covers a KO event re-simulated by a correction. No test covers the view side: ArenaScene's one-shot flashes keyed by event id (apps/web/src/arenaScene.ts), or DuelClient's pendingEvents buffer, which is capped at 32 (apps/web/src/duelClient.ts:139-144). So nothing shows the view does not show an event twice.

# Task: duel

## Goal

Deliver the `duel-online` combat spike with its review findings fixed. Run duel-online-001 built it and passed every check: 32 integration tests, and a harness at 80 ms / 20 ms / 1 % with 0 desyncs over 181 hash checks and 0 rate-limited drops. But its coverage reviewer blocked the candidate, because nothing tests the dev latency setting the operator's playtest depends on, and its general reviewer never finished. Start from that run's snapshot, then close the findings below so that the whole feature can be reviewed again.

## Context

- `features/duel-online/duel-task.md` and `features/duel-online/decisions.md` define the feature, and all of it still applies. Read them first.
- **First step:** restore duel-online-001's snapshot into your worktree with `git checkout refs/workflow/9d324071c360f7c2/duel -- .` (commit `cb8fe85`). It changes only paths this lane owns. Then read `docs/duel.md` and `docs/architecture.md`.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration`, `npm run build` and `npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`. Playwright's Chromium for `@playwright/test` 1.63.0 is installed and shared read-only; never run `playwright install`.
- Other features (`claim-channel`, `objectives-ledger`) are already on `main` and will be merged with this one afterwards. Don't recreate them here.
- **This machine is shared by several runs. Never stop processes by name pattern (`pkill -f`, `killall`, and so on): `pkill -f vite` also matched another run's `vitest` and failed its verification. Stop only the PIDs you started.**

Findings to fix (coverage reviewer unless noted):

1. (P1) The dev latency setting's behaviour has no test. `apps/web/src/duel.test.ts` only parses the query, and the smoke check only proves the setting is absent from the production bundle. The browser checks run that production build, so prove the behaviour below the browser:
   - unit tests (fake timers) show that `applyDevLatency` / `DelayLine` (`apps/web/src/devLatency.ts`) delay outgoing and incoming messages, probes included, by about RTT/2 each way, add bounded jitter, and never reorder;
   - an integration test wraps a headless duel client's transport in that same module (import it from `apps/web/src`; keep it free of DOM dependencies so Node can load it) and shows that the room's measured round trip and its chosen input delay rise above the no-latency case.
2. (P2) Nothing asserts that input-delay selection follows measured latency. The harness only prints `inputDelay`. Assert it: the minimum with no impairment, and a delay inside the expected band above the minimum at 80 ms / 20 ms / 1 %.
3. (P2) The HUD's stamina display (`apps/web/src/duelHud.ts`) is never read by a test. Assert it in a browser scenario (for example after a dash) and in a unit test.
4. (P2) The resync-after-stall test (`packages/simulation/src/netcode/netcode.test.ts`) ends with `expect(bundle).toBeDefined()` and never checks the restored state. Assert that the session's confirmed state equals the authority's after `resync()`. Add the case the requirement names: contiguous bundles keep arriving while ticks stall, as in a hidden tab.
5. (P2) Stable-id de-duplication is tested only for a hit at the rollback level. Add a KO re-simulated by a correction, and a view-side test showing that the arena and the client's pending-event buffer show each event once.
6. (P2, assistant's review) When both players are absent and their reconnection windows expire, the first `onLeave` awards the win to the other absent player (`apps/server/src/DuelRoom.ts`, around lines 181–184). §12 says to cancel: when the opponent is also disconnected, end the duel with no winner. Add an integration test.
7. (P2, assistant's review) When the phase becomes "over", the client stops ticking (`apps/web/src/duelClient.ts`, around line 129), so the HUD's result, clock and health can trail the final bundle. Keep stepping to the last bundle's frame.
8. (P2, assistant's review) `DuelInputGate` copies the world `InputGate`'s rate and validation logic. Share it (for example a common rate window) so they cannot drift, keeping `InputGate`'s behaviour and tests unchanged.

## Constraints

- Owned paths as in `policy.json`. Apart from restoring the snapshot, change only what the findings need, and keep the existing structure, names and patterns.
- The duel rules stay untouched, as in `features/duel-online/duel-task.md`. Keep the protocol version, the six browser scenario ids and every existing test.
- Tests drive input like players do.

## Acceptance

- The restored `duel-online` feature meets all of `features/duel-online/duel-task.md`'s acceptance.
- Findings 1–8 are fixed with the tests they name. The dev latency tests fail if the delay, the jitter bound or the ordering breaks. The input-delay assertions fail if the chosen delay ignores measured latency.
- The integration suite stays well inside its 300-second check timeout.
- `npm ci` then each of the five policy checks passes from a clean checkout.

Browser checks: each scenario id appears in exactly one test title as `[scenario:<id>]`. That test, when it passes, attaches exactly one image/png named `screenshot:<id>` (other attachments are fine). The verifier refuses anything else. Before completing, run the spec files you changed with a JSON report:

```bash
WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=worker PLAYWRIGHT_JSON_OUTPUT_FILE=<tmp>/report.json \
  npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts --reporter=json <spec files>
```

Then check the report with the verifier's own rules: run the exact `check-report` command the controller appends to this task when it pins it.

## Stop

Report `blocked` instead of continuing when any of these happens:

- Restoring the snapshot fails or touches a path outside the owned paths.
- `npm ci` or an install fails twice for reasons outside the repository (registry, network).
- A check can pass only by changing a path outside the owned paths.
- After two hours of work, any required check still fails and you cannot name the next fix.

Report `question` only for a choice that would change this acceptance.

lastPrompt: Can you tell me why are we facing this many errros in the workflow?

content.text:
I went back through today's runs and logs. The failures fall into a few distinct causes, and most of them are fixable at the source.

**The scorecard:** 9 runs finished. **6 were approved first time**, 3 were blocked in review, and 2 verifications failed for reasons unrelated to the code under test. Five design challenges paused.

### 1. Review blocks: under-specified test requirements (the most costly)
| Run | Blocked by | What was missing |
|---|---|---|
| skeleton-001 | general + coverage | A real security hole (joining without a code), plus no proof the built server runs |
| world-sea-001 | coverage | No test that the map is actually drawn |
| duel-online-001 | coverage | No test that the dev latency setting works |

The last two had **nothing wrong with the code**. The `coverage` reviewer blocks when an acceptance item isn't *proven* by a test. My task files described features ("the client draws the map", "a dev latency setting") without saying which test proves each one, so the workers tested what was easy.

**Fix:** every acceptance bullet names the test that would fail if it broke. I'll write tasks that way from now on.

### 2. The controller amplifies each review block
- **One reviewer blocks, the other is cut off.** The first block stops the second reviewer, so the general review never happened for world-sea or duel-online. That forced a *second full review* of the whole feature.
- **A block after review means a whole new feature.** `repair` isn't allowed once review has started, so even a test-only gap costs a new run: a challenge, a worker and two reviews, roughly 40–60 minutes.

**Fix (md-manager):** let every reviewer finish, and allow a repair after review for test-only findings. That would turn these blocks into roughly 10-minute fixes.

### 3. Design-challenge pauses: my plans had gaps
There were five: skeleton-fixes (seat squatting), duel-core (build proof), duel-online (input rate cap, duplicated rollback logic), and duel-online-fixes (I misread §12's forfeit rule).

These are the challenge **doing its job**. Each cost 2–5 minutes, where the same mistakes found by a worker or reviewer would have cost an hour. They trace back to me writing decisions from recommended defaults without a real grill. Grilling with you on the risky choices would catch some of them earlier.

### 4. Environment and tooling (fixed or avoidable)
- **Verifier couldn't read Vitest output** (skeleton-001). Fixed in md-manager this morning.
- **A shared machine hurt:** the duel worker's `pkill -f "vite"` killed the ledger's verification. Now forbidden in tasks; it should go into `CLAUDE.md` too.
- **Ctrl-C during the silent challenge** twice. The challenge runs as a headless job that prints nothing for minutes. **Fix:** give it a pane, as you asked earlier.

### 5. Bugs the checks couldn't see
Docking passed every check and two reviews but failed your first playtest, because the tests used idealised input. It's in memory: tests must press keys the way players do.

### What I'd change, in order of payoff
1. **Task template:** "each acceptance item names the test that proves it; screenshots and bookkeeping attributes don't count." This removes most review blocks.
2. **md-manager:** all reviewers finish, and test-only findings can be repaired after review.
3. **Grill with you** on the risky design choices, instead of me defaulting them.
4. **`CLAUDE.md`:** no `pkill -f` or `killall`, and stop dev servers before launches.
5. **Challenge in a pane**, so a quiet challenge is never mistaken for a hang.

Items 1 and 4 are quick edits in this repo that I can make now. Item 2, and item 5 in md-manager, need changes to md-manager, and those have to wait until no run is live. Want me to go ahead with 1 and 4?

The failure, from the run's browser report: in `sail-and-dock` the ship reaches the dock and the HUD hint shows it's in reach (that assertion passed), but **holding E for 10 s never docks it**. The HUD stays at "at sea".

My guess, going only by the task: finding 8 asked the worker to share the input gate's logic, and that gate holds the button latch that makes E reliable.

What happens next:
- **The candidate gate re-runs the browser suite.** If `sail-and-dock` passes there, it was a one-off.

130	  const { HeadlessClient } = await import("@pirate-sea-race/test-tools");
131	  const { TEST_PLACEMENT_PATH } = await import("@pirate-sea-race/protocol");
132	  const host = await withTimeout(HeadlessClient.create(endpoint), MATCH_TIMEOUT_MS, "creating a match");
133	  try {
134	    const ship = host.ship();
135	    if (!/^[A-Z0-9]{6}$/.test(host.code)) throw new Error(`the match has no code (got "${host.code}")`);
136	    if (ship === undefined || host.playerCount !== 1) throw new Error("the creator's ship is not in the match state");
137	    log(`created match ${host.code}; the creator's ship is at (${ship.x}, ${ship.y})`);
138	    // The production entry never reads the test-placement setting, even when the environment sets it.
139	    const response = await fetch(`${endpoint}${TEST_PLACEMENT_PATH}`, {
140	      method: "POST",
141	      headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
142	      body: JSON.stringify({ code: host.code, sessionId: host.sessionId, tileX: 100, tileY: 76, heading: 0 }),
143	      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS),
144	    });
145	    if (response.status !== 404) throw new Error(`the production server answered the test placement route with HTTP ${response.status}`);
146	    log("the production server offers no test placement");
147	  } finally {
148	    await withTimeout(host.leave(), STOP_TIMEOUT_MS, "leaving the match").catch(() => undefined);
149	  }
150	}
151	
152	/** A practice duel on the built server: the built rollback core confirms frames and agrees with every server hash. */
153	async function openPracticeDuel(endpoint: string): Promise<void> {
154	  const { HeadlessDuelClient } = await import("@pirate-sea-race/test-tools");
155	  const player = await withTimeout(HeadlessDuelClient.create(endpoint, { practice: true }), MATCH_TIMEOUT_MS, "creating a practice duel");
156	  try {
157	    await withTimeout(player.waitForConfirmed(30, DUEL_TIMEOUT_MS), DUEL_TIMEOUT_MS + 1000, "the practice duel's first frames");
158	    const stats = player.stats!;
159	    if (stats.hashChecks === 0 || stats.desyncs !== 0) throw new Error(`the practice duel's hash checks: ${JSON.stringify(stats)}`);
160	    log(`practice duel ${player.code}: frame ${player.duel!.rollback.confirmedFrame} confirmed, ${stats.hashChecks} hash checks, no desync`);
161	  } finally {
162	    await withTimeout(player.leave(), STOP_TIMEOUT_MS, "leaving the duel").catch(() => undefined);
163	  }
164	}
165	
166	/** Stops the server: SIGTERM lets it drain; SIGKILL follows if it does not exit in time. */
167	async function stopServer(): Promise<void> {
168	  const child = server;
169	  if (child === undefined || !running(child)) return;
170	  const exited = new Promise<void>((resolve) => child.once("exit", () => resolve()));
171	  child.kill("SIGTERM");
172	  await withTimeout(exited, STOP_TIMEOUT_MS, "server shutdown").catch(async () => {
173	    child.kill("SIGKILL");
174	    await withTimeout(exited, STOP_TIMEOUT_MS, "killing the server");
175	  });
176	}
177	
178	// Last resort for paths that skip `finally`: an exit, or a signal from whoever runs the build.
179	process.once("exit", () => {
180	  if (server !== undefined && running(server)) server.kill("SIGKILL");
181	});
182	for (const signal of ["SIGINT", "SIGTERM"] as const) {
183	  process.once(signal, () => {
184	    console.error(`build smoke: interrupted by ${signal}`);
185	    process.exit(1);
186	  });
187	}
188	
189	async function main(): Promise<void> {
190	  await checkWorkspaceExports();
191	  await checkWebBundle();
192	  const port = await startServer();
193	  const endpoint = `http://localhost:${port}`;
194	  log(`${SERVER_ENTRY} listens on port ${port}`);
195	  await waitForHealth(endpoint);
196	  log("health check answers");
197	  await createMatch(endpoint);
198	  await openPracticeDuel(endpoint);
199	}
200	
201	let failed = false;
202	try {
203	  await withTimeout(main(), OVERALL_TIMEOUT_MS, "the build smoke test");
204	  log("passed");
205	} catch (error) {
206	  failed = true;
207	  console.error("build smoke: FAILED");
208	  console.error(error);
209	} finally {
210	  await stopServer().catch((error: unknown) => {
211	    failed = true;
212	    console.error("build smoke: could not stop the server", error);
213	  });
214	}
215	process.exit(failed ? 1 : 0);
216
